statement: Let A ̸= 0 be separable with dimnuc A ≤ d < ∞. 1. If no hereditary subalgebra of A has a finite-dimensional irreducible representation, then there are finitely many finite-dimensional algebras Ej, completely positive order-zero maps φj : Ej → F(A), and elements cj ∈ F(A) such that every matrix summand of every Ej has size at least two and 1F(A) = X j c∗ j φj(1Ej )cj. This is the matrix-threshold-two consequence of the covering-number bound cov(F(A)) ≤ (d + 1)2 [WZ2, Definition 4.1 and Proposition 4.3]. 2. If F(A) contains two full orthogonal positive elements, then A ∼ = A⊗min Z [RT, Theorem 1.2]. Both assertions apply to nonunital A, with the annihilator quotient just defined.
